title: test_call_time_binding declares PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 900, so its 284 s wall is not read as a 120 s timeout
intention: The call-time binding proof declares its own time limit above its measured wall, so a reseal that touches proof_coverage runs it to a verdict instead of timing it out and leaving its seal standing over an old fingerprint.
why: Measured 2026-11-22: the b64847df255d build commit's reseal printed 'TIMEOUT cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_call_time_binding.py (timed out after 120s under isolation none)'; a timed run on house main went green in 284 s wall at load 2.2. It declares no PROOF_TIMEOUT_S, so the reseal's 120 s default applies to every reseal touching proof_coverage.
traces_to: Law 9 (green is earned) and Law 3 (the budget follows the measured wall)
how: Add a top-level PROOF_TIMEOUT_S = 900 to cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_call_time_binding.py: 3.2x the 284 s wall, room for a loaded box (walls here roughly double under load). The mechanism is 8383a32d20c5's; the red-first proof copies 6437cfd935bb's cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_the_census_proof_declares_a_budget_above_its_wall.py retargeted at cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_call_time_binding.py.

under cairn test with a caller budget below a scratch fixture's run, the fixture carrying the declared value finishes green; the same fixture undeclared, or declared below its run, does not, so the declared value and not the caller's budget is the run's budget
